15.text:
Basket A is degenerate.  On the conventional finance reading a “constant
growth rate’’ is a geometric drift

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\qquad {\rm a.s.}$

so that after the 30 y hold and the essentially free liquidation in the
31st year

$V^{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\qquad {\rm a.s.},\qquad 
E[V^{A}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$.

Basket B is specified as a non-seasonal ARIMA with drift, i.e. a level
random walk with drift

$\Delta P^{B}_{t}= \mu+\varepsilon_{t},\qquad E[\varepsilon_{t}]=0,$

$P^{B}_{t}=P_{0}+\mu t+\sum_{s\le t}\varepsilon_{s}.$

A “linear growth trend of $10\%$ each year’’ in the ARIMA sense is an
additive level drift,
$\mu=0.10P_{0}$, so that in levels

$E\big[P^{B}_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}\big]=P^{B}_{s}+\mu(t-s),\qquad
E\big[P^{B}_{t}\big]=P_{0}+\mu t=P_{0}\big[1+0.10t\big].$

The level trend is therefore arithmetic, $1+0.10t$, not the geometric
$1.10^{t}$ of A.  In particular

$E[P^{B}_{30}]=P_{0}[1+3.0]=4P_{0}\ll P_{0}1.10^{30}\simeq17.45P_{0}$,

and for any ${\cal F}$-adapted admissible liquidation $Q_{t}$,
$Q_{30}=0,Q_{31}=1$,

$V^{B}_{Q}= \int_{30}^{31}P^{B}_{t}\,dQ_{t}
          =-P_{30}+ \int_{30}^{31}H_{t}\,dP^{B}_{t},$

$H_{t}=1-Q_{t}$.  With $dP^{B}_{t}=\mu dt+dM_{t}$, $M$ a zero-mean
martingale, $E\big[\int H_{t}dM_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]=0$ for
predictable $H$.  Hence

$E\big[V^{B}_{Q}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]
 =-P_{30}+ \mu\int_{30}^{31}E\big[H_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]dt
 \le -P_{30}+ \mu(31-30)
 =E\big[P^{B}_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big],$

with equality only for the buy-and-hold-to-the-end policy $H_{t}\equiv1$.
The drift is positive, so waiting is mean optimal; the $O(\sigma)$
$E[\sup P^{B}_{t}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$ look-back effect is not attainable by a
feasible non-anticipative liquidation rule, and the martingale part has
zero mean.

Hence for every admissible liquidation rule

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]
 \le E[P^{B}_{31}]
 =P_{0}\big[1+0.10\times31\big]
 \ll P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}]$,

and indeed

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]=O(P_{0}+\mu31)\ll P_{0}1.10^{31}.$

The $20\%$ weekly moves give dispersion, so $V^{B}$ can on a path be
above or below $V^{A}$; E and H are false.  Both price processes have
the $10\%$ drift, they are strict sub-martingales, not martingales, so
B,C,D,F are false.  In unconditional mean the deterministic compound
basket strictly dominates the additive-drift ARIMA random walk, i.e. the
statement

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket B,

is the strict mean ordering implied by the arithmetic-versus-geometric
growth distinction that the “linear growth trend’’ / ARIMA-with-drift
wording is intended to make.  Under the textbook geometric-drift
reading of B the passive means coincide and the intra-year timing option
gives the familiar $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}]$, i.e. G, but under the
literal level-linear ARIMA specification the exponential mean of A
dominates the linear mean of B in expectation.

3.text:
Basket A and basket B are not on the same mean scale.

On the wording that is used for B the 10% p.a. is an additive level drift.
An ARIMA$(0,1,0)$ with drift in levels is

$\Delta S^{B}_{t}= \mu +\varepsilon_{t},\qquad  E \varepsilon_{t}=0 ,$
$\mu =0.10\,S_{0}$,

so that in levels

$E\big[S^{B}_{t}\big]=S_{0}+\mu t=S_{0}\big[1+0.10t\big],$

with constant autocovariance for the de-meaned increments.  The $20\%$
weekly moves are the martingale part of the walk; they change dispersion
only.

Basket A is described as a constant $10\%$ p.a. growth rate with no noise.
On the finance reading that is the compound law

$S^{A}_{t}=S_{0}(1.10)^{t}\;\;{\rm a.s.},$

and with the 30 y buy-and-hold and a deterministic liquidation in the
31st year

$V^{A}=S_{0}(1.10)^{31}\quad {\rm a.s.},\qquad 
E[V^{A}]=S_{0}(1.10)^{31}.$

In particular

$E\big[S^{B}_{30}\big]=S_{0}(1+3.0)=4S_{0}\ll S_{0}(1.10)^{30}\approx17.45S_{0},
$

$E\big[S^{B}_{31}\big]=S_{0}(1+3.1)=4.10S_{0}\ll S_{0}(1.10)^{31}\approx19.2S_{0},$

so that even the passive mean of B is $O(S_{0}+\mu t)$ whereas the mean of
A is $O\big(S_{0}1.10^{t}\big)$.
For any ${\cal F}$-adapted admissible liquidation $q_{t}\ge0$,
$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$,

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}S^{B}_{t}dt\right]
 =\int_{30}^{31}E[q_{t}]E[S^{B}_{t}]dt+{\rm Cov} $

and for the additive drifted walk the conditional mean satisfies
$E[S^{B}_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=S^{B}_{s}+\mu(t-s)$, i.e. $S^{B}$ is a
strict sub-martingale in levels.  The unconditional mean of any
predictable liquidation is therefore bounded by the terminal mean,

$E[V^{B}_{\tau}]\le E\big[S^{B}_{31}\big]=S_{0}+31\mu ,$

with equality for the mean-optimal policy $\tau\equiv31$, and the
$O(\sigma)$ look-back premium $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}S^{B}_{t}]>E[S^{B}_{31}]$
is not attainable by a single non-anticipative liquidation rule.  Hence

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}] = O\big(S_{0}+31\mu\big)\ll S_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}].$

The dominance is in mean only.  The $20\%$ weekly volatility gives B a
non-negligible right tail, so on a realised path $V^{B}$ can be above
$V^{A}$; E and H are false.  The price processes are strict sub-martingales
with $10\%$ drift, not martingales, so B,C,D,F are false.  In unconditional
mean the deterministic compound basket strictly dominates the additive-drift
random walk, i.e. the statement

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket B,

which is the $A>B$ in-expectation ordering under the literal ARIMA-with-drift
additive $10\%$ p.a. trend that is written for B.  On the usual geometric-drift
reading $E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}1.10^{t}$ the passive means coincide and the
intra-year timing/look-back option makes $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}]$,
the G ordering quoted by the majority of the group. ∎

6.text:
Basket A is deterministic on the liquidation window. On the literal wording
$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t\;$ a.s. so that for any admissible
$[30,31]$-liquidation

$V^{A}=P^{A}_{31}=P_{0}\bigl[1+0.10\times 31\bigr]\qquad{\rm a.s.}$
and $E[V^{A}]=V^{A}$.  Intra-year timing is irrelevant for A.

Write the B level on the 31st year as
$P^{B}_{30+s}=P^{B}_{30}+ \mu s+M_{s}$ with $\mu =0.10P_{0}>0$ and
$M_{s}$ a zero-mean martingale with constant long run volatility,
$\sigma_{w}=20\%$ per week.  Hence in mean

$E\!\left[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\right]=P^{B}_{t}+\mu\Delta>P^{B}_{t}$,
so $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the same $10\%$ p.a. linear
drift as A.  For a fixed horizon $E[P^{B}_{T}]=E[P^{A}_{T}]$; de-meaned
returns are stationary but the price processes are not martingales.
B, C, D and F are therefore false.

Let $q_{t}\ge0$, $\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, be ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted and
$V^{B}_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt$.  With the drift the mean of
any adapted schedule is maximised by delaying sales, i.e. in the limit

$V^{B*}\approx \sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\quad{\rm a.s.}$

with strict inequality on a set of positive probability as soon as
$\sigma_{B}>0$.  The 31st year liquidation window is an American
look-back/timing option on the volatile component of B.  In
expectation

$E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]>E\!\left[P^{B}_{31}\right]
   =E\!\left[P^{A}_{31}\right]=V^{A},$

so the optimally timed mean liquidation value of the volatile drifted
basket is strictly larger than the deterministic mean liquidation value
of A,

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]
   >E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[V^{A}].$

The gain is the classic convex volatility/timing premium,
$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]=E[P^{B}_{31}]+{\rm OptionValue}(\sigma_{B}>0)>E[P^{A}_{31}]$.
It is in mean only: $P^{B}$ can realise paths well below $P^{A}$ so the
necessarily higher statements E and H are false, and the passive mean
holds $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$.

Hence on the linear-price / linear-trend reading that the statement
makes explicit the strictly expected-value ordering is the volatile
basket dominates the deterministic one by the intra-year timing option,
i.e. 

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

with the usual caveat that the outperformance is expectation only and
that the $A>B$ reading is recovered only if A is re-interpreted as the
geometric compound $P_{0}1.10^{t}$ while B is kept additive linear,
$E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$.

12.text:
The wording is the key.

A is described as a constant 10% p.a. growth rate with no noise. In
finance a constant percentage growth rate is geometric,
$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s., and the “completely linear with no
noise’’ reading is the deterministic-path reading.  With the 30 y hold
and a deterministic unwind in the 31st year

$V^{A}_{opt}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\qquad{\rm a.s.},\qquad
E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}.$

B is explicitly an ARIMA with drift, i.e. a random walk around a mean
with drift.  In levels

$S^{B}_{t}=S_{0}+\mu t+\eta_{t},\qquad 
E[\eta_{t}]=0,\qquad \mu=0.10S_{0},$

so that in mean

$E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+\mu t=S_{0}\!\left[1+0.10t\right],$

an arithmetic linear trend.  For any ${\cal F}$-adapted liquidation
weight $w_{s}\ge0$, $\int_{30}^{31}w_{s}ds=1$,

$E[V^{B}_{w}]
 =\int_{30}^{31} w_{s}E[S^{B}_{30+s}]ds
 \le E[S^{B}_{31}]
 =S_{0}\!\left[1+0.10\times31\right]
 \ll S_{0}1.10^{31}$.

The intra-year timing option can be written as
$\int w_{s}S^{B}_{30+s}ds = \int w_{s}\bigl[S_{0}+\mu(30+s)\bigr]ds+
\int w_{s}\eta_{30+s}ds$.
With $H_{t}=\int_{30}^{t}w_{s}ds$,
$\int w_{s}\eta_{30+s}ds=H_{t}\eta_{t}-\int H_{t}d\eta_{t}$ and the
martingale part has zero mean, so

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31} w_{s}\eta_{30+s}ds\right]=0$.

Hence $E[V^{B}_{opt}]=O\!\left(S_{0}+\mu31\right)$ and the $O(\sigma)$
look-back $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}S^{B}_{t}]>E[S^{B}_{31}]$ is not
attainable by a non-anticipative unwind; waiting is mean optimal for a
level sub-martingale.  In particular

$E[S^{B}_{30}]=4S_{0}\ll S_{0}1.10^{30}\approx17.45S_{0},$

so the exponential mean of the geometric basket A can never be closed
by the $O(\sigma)$ timing premium of the additive-drift walk.

Hence in unconditional mean

$E[V^{A}]=S_{0}1.10^{31}>E[V^{B}_{opt}]$,

i.e. the deterministic compound basket strictly dominates the
additive-drift ARIMA basket in expectation.  The dominance is only in
mean: with $20\%$ weekly moves $S^{B}$ has a heavy right tail and can
realise a terminal value above $V^{A}$ on a given $\omega$, so E and H
are false.  Both price processes have the 10% drift and are
sub-martingales in levels, so B,C,D,F are false.  The strictly
expected-value ordering is

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket B,

the arithmetic-vs-geometric growth distinction that the ARIMA-with-drift
specification for B is intended to make.  The passive-mean equality
$E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}+ \mu31$ is the source of the $G$ votes; it holds
only for the arithmetic reading of A.

9.text:
Basket A is degenerate under the usual finance reading of a 10% p.a.
drift.  In price terms

$E[P^{A}_{t+\Delta}\mid {\cal F}_{t}]=P^{A}_{t}1.10^{\Delta},\qquad 
P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\ {\rm a.s.}$

so that on a passive hold

$V^{A}_{opt}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\ {\rm a.s.},\qquad 
E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$.

Basket B is the same drifted sub–martingale with $\sigma_{B}>0$,

$E[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=P^{B}_{t}1.10^{\Delta},\qquad 
E[P^{B}_{T}]=P_{0}1.10^{T},$

i.e. the two baskets have the same first moment on a fixed horizon.
The 31st year is an $[30,31]$ liquidation window.  Let $q_{t}\ge0$,
$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, be ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted.  In the limit the
attainable liquidation value is the running maximum on the window

$V^{B}_{opt}(\omega)\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}(\omega)\ge
P^{B}_{31}(\omega)\ {\rm a.s.}$

and $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the 10% drift and
$\sigma_{B}>0$.  Hence

$E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]>E[P^{B}_{31}]
      =P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}],$

the strict inequality being the familiar American / look-back premium.
Making the sales flow positively correlated with the price path makes the
realised proceeds stochastically larger than the deterministic A value,
so that in expectation

$E[V^{B}_{opt}]\ge E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}]
      >P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}].$

The out-performance is in mean only.  On a realised path
$V^{B}_{opt}$ can be far below $V^{A}$, so E and H are false, and $P^{A},
P^{B}$ are strict sub-martingales with a 10% drift, not martingales, so
B,C,D,F are false.  With the 10% p.a. compound drift reading that the
group has adopted the strictly expected-value ordering is therefore

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

the passive-mean equality $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ being the
baseline and the excess being the value of the intra-year timing /
volatility option that A does not possess.  On the literal additive
linear-price reading $E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$ versus
$S^{A}_{t}=S_{0}1.10^{t}$ the exponential versus linear gap gives the
A-dominance reading.

2.text:
The 10 % p.a. has to be read in the usual finance sense as a geometric
drift

$E\big[P_{t+\Delta}\mid {\cal F}_{t}\big]=P_{t}1.10^{\Delta},$

i.e. $E[P_{t}]=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ for both baskets on a passive hold.
On that reading $P^{A}$ is the degenerate sub-martingale

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\qquad {\rm a.s.}$

so that with a $30\,{\rm y}$ buy-and-hold and a deterministic unwind in
year $31$

$V^{A}_{opt}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\qquad {\rm a.s.},\qquad 
E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}1.10^{31},$

and any intra-year timing is irrelevant for $A$.
$P^{B}$ has the same $10\%$ p.a. mean drift but $\sigma_{B}>0$ with
constant long run volatility.  In price terms

$E\big[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{B}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}>P^{B}_{t},$

so $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale, not a martingale, and on a fixed
horizon $E[P^{B}_{T}]=P_{0}1.10^{T}=E[P^{A}_{T}]$.  The 31st year is an
adapted liquidation window $[30,31]$.  For an ${\cal F}$-adapted
selling schedule $q_{t}\ge0$, $\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$,

$V^{B}_{q}= \int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt,$

and the convex timing payoff can be made positively correlated with the
price path.  In the limit

$V^{B}_{opt}\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\quad {\rm a.s.}$

with strict inequality on a set of positive probability as soon as
$\sigma_{B}>0$.  Hence for a non-degenerate drifted process

$E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le 31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]>E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]
     =P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}],$

i.e. the 31st year liquidation window is a strictly positive American /
look-back option on $B$.  On a passive hold the two baskets have the
same first moment, $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$, so $P^{B}$ is a
sub-martingale with a $10\%$ drift and the martingale / stationary-return
statements B,C,D,F are false.  The outperformance is in expectation only:
on a realised $\omega$ $P^{B}$ can finish arbitrarily far below $P^{A}$,
so the necessarily higher statements E and H are false.

On the usual geometric-drift convention the strictly
expected-value ordering is therefore

$E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[V^{A}_{opt}],$

the textbook volatility / timing option value of $B$ over the
deterministic $A$.  That is the statement

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

with the usual caveat that the dominance is only in mean and a realised
$B$ path can be below $A$.  Remark: on the literal additive ARIMA-with-drift
reading $E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$ the mean of $B$ is arithmetic
whereas $A$ is usually read as geometric $S_{0}1.10^{t}$ and the
exponential versus linear gap gives $E[V^{A}]\gg E[V^{B}_{opt}]$, i.e. the
$A$-dominance reading.

8.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the liquidation window.  Write the 31st year
as $30+s,\;0\le s\le 1$.  On the literal linear price reading

$P_{t}^{A}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t\;\;a.s.$

so that with a deterministic price any admissible liquidation plan on
$[30,31]$ satisfies

$V^{A}=P_{31}^{A}=P_{0}\bigl[1+0.10\times31\bigr]\qquad a.s.$

and $E[V^{A}]=V^{A}$.  In levels

$P_{t}^{B}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t+M_{t}, \qquad E[M_{t}]=0,$

with $M_{t}$ a zero mean martingale with constant long run variance,
$E[\,P_{t}^{B}\mid{\cal F}_{s}\,]=P_{s}^{B}+0.10P_{0}(t-s)>P_{s}^{B}$.
Hence $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the same $10\%$ p.a. linear
drift in the mean as $A$ and $E[P_{T}^{B}]=E[P_{T}^{A}]$ for every fixed
$T$ on a passive hold-to-maturity.

On $[30,31]$ let $q_{t}\ge0,\;\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$ be an
${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted liquidation density and
$V_{q}^{B}=\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P_{t}^{B}dt$.  With
$A_{t}=\int_{30}^{t}q_{s}ds$,

$V_{q}^{B}= \int_{30}^{31}q_{t}\bigl[P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t\bigr]dt
         +\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}dq_{t}$,

and $E[\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}dq_{t}]=0$.  The mean part is
$E[V_{q}^{B}]=\int_{30}^{31}E[q_{t}]\,[P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t]dt$, so that
for a fixed horizon the mean of any adapted plan is maximised by
postponing sales.  The unconstrained ex-post value that can be
identified with the liquidation window is the running maximum

$V^{B,*}\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_{t}^{B}\ge P_{31}^{B}\;\;a.s.,$

and for a non-degenerate sub-martingale with $\sigma_{B}>0$

$E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_{t}^{B}\right]
   >E\!\left[P_{31}^{B}\right]=E\!\left[P_{31}^{A}\right]=V^{A},$

the strict inequality being the usual volatility/timing/ look-back
premium created by the $20\%$ weekly moves in the 31st year.  Hence

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_{t}^{B}\right]
   >E[P_{31}^{B}]=E[V^{A}]$,

i.e. the volatile drifted basket commands a strictly positive
American/optimal-stopping value over the deterministic linear basket.
The out-performance is mean only: $P^{B}$ can realise a path that
finishes well below $P^{A}$, so the necessarily-higher statements E
and H are false.  The price processes are sub-martingales with a $10\%$
drift, not martingales, so B,C,D,F are false and the deterministic
dominance A is false once the intra-year timing option is accounted
for.  The strongest true statement in the list is the strict
expected-value dominance of the volatile basket

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

with $E[V^{B}_{\rm passive}]=E[V^{A}]$ and the excess being the value of
the $31^{\rm st}$-year look-back / timing option.  On the
conventional geometric $P_{0}1.10^{t}$ reading for A the additive
ARIMA-with-drift mean of B is $P_{0}[1+0.10t]$ and the ordering flips to
$E[V^{A}]>E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]$, i.e. the A statement, which is the
exponential vs. linear artefact noted by colleagues 7,10,12,15.

public_text.13:
I think the intra-year option value story is being overstated because it is not a feasible stopping time under the wording of the liquidation rule.

The price of A is described as “completely linear with no noise.” That is a level process
P_t^A = P0 + 0.10 P0 t a.s. on the 30 y horizon.  For B the specification is a non-seasonal ARIMA with drift, constant autocovariance and a linear growth trend of 10 % each year.  In levels that is
E[ΔP_t^B | F_{t-1}] = μ = 0.10 P0 ,   E[P_t^B] = P0 + μ t ,
i.e. an additive linear mean. After de-meaning the drift the return increments are stationary with constant autocovariance, which is exactly the statement in the problem.

Hence on a fixed horizon both baskets have the same first moment
E[P_t^B] = P_t^A = P0 + 0.10 P0 t .
Both are sub-martingales with the same 10 % arithmetic drift; neither is a martingale in price terms.

Liquidation in the 31st year is “over the course of the 31st year with whatever liquidation strategy will maximize value.” That is a predictable, non-anticipative unwind, not a single stopping time.  For an adapted weight process w_s ≥ 0, ∫_0^1 w_s ds = 1,

E[V^B] = E[ ∫_0^1 w_s P_{30+s}^B ds ] = ∫_0^1 w_s E[ P_{30+s}^B ] ds
       = ∫_0^1 w_s [ P0 + 0.10 P0 (30+s) ] ds .

By the tower property the unconditional mean of the integral is the integral of the unconditional means.  The martingale part of B has zero mean,  E[∫ q_t dW_t]=0, so the only thing that moves the first moment is the drift μ.  With a positive drift the mean-optimal predictable plan is to postpone weight as much as the admissible policy allows, i.e. in the limit to hold to the end of the window.  You can correlate w_s with the path and you will change the distribution of the realised proceeds and you will get an ex-post timing premium, but you cannot change the unconditional mean of an adapted integral against a process with stationary, drifted increments.

The pathwise supremum sup_{30≤t≤31} P_t^B is indeed stochastically larger than P_{31}^B and E[sup P] > E[P_{31}]. That supremum is an ex-post hindsight quantity. It is not the expectation of any single feasible year-long unwind of a finite position. A feasible unwind averages price over the year, and averaging is linear in expectation.  In expectation the optimal adapted liquidation value of B is therefore pinned by the drift mean,

E[V^B_opt] = E[P_{31}^B] = P0 + 0.10 P0 × 31 = V^A .

Volatility creates dispersion and a realisation-by-realisation timing illusion, it does not create an ex-ante mean premium.  That is why the first-moment statement is the same for the two baskets: the return distribution is stationary after removing the known 10 % drift, so the expected liquidation wealth is pinned by the drift alone.

In that sense the strongest claim that remains true under the stated ARIMA-with-drift, linear-price specification and a year-long gradual unwind is that the unconditional expected values coincide.  The necessarily-higher claims E and H are false, and the strict expected dominance G relies on treating the 31st year as a free American look-back that can be exercised with hindsight, which is not attainable by a feasible, predictable liquidation schedule over the course of the year.
public_text.14:
I think the G camp is right about the convexity intuition and wrong about what can actually be locked in.

Yes for basket B with σ>0 we have E[ sup_{30≤t≤31} P_t^B ] > E[P_{31}^B] . That is a true ex-post inequality, and it is what makes the look-back argument feel compelling. The problem is that sup_{t} P_t is not an attainable ex-ante liquidation value when liquidation has to happen “over the course of the 31st year”.

Any admissible year-long unwind is a predictable weight process q_t ≥0 with ∫_{30}^{31} q_t dt =1. Realised proceeds are V =∫ q_t P_t^B dt. By tower property

E[V] = E[ ∫ q_t E[P_t^B | F_t] dt ] = ∫ E[ q_t E[P_t^B | F_t] ] dt .

For both baskets the 10% p.a. trend is the same drift in price terms,
E[P_{t+Δ}|F_t] = P_t 1.10^{Δ}, and after de-meaning the increments are stationary. 
In particular for a fixed horizon E[P_T^B]=P0 1.10^T =E[P_T^A] and P^B is a sub-martingale with the same mean drift as A.

If you try to make q_t positively correlated with P_t you do change the distribution of V, you do create a right tail, but you do not change its unconditional mean. For a sub-martingale with positive drift waiting is mean increasing, E[P_τ|F_30] ≤ E[P_31|F_30] for τ≤31, and for any predictable q

E[∫ q_t P_t dt] = ∫ q_t E[P_t] dt ≤ E[P_31] ,

with equality in the limit q_t → δ_{31}. The averaging inherent in a year-long unwind is linear in expectation. The pathwise maximum that colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,11 quote is an ex-post hindsight quantity; it is not the expectation of any single adapted liquidation schedule that unwinds a finite position gradually. You cannot sell the whole position at the running maximum without knowing the maximum in advance.

Hence on an unconditional ex-ante basis the two strategies have the same first moment. Volatility changes dispersion, the shape of the distribution and the ex-post timing premium, it does not create a mean premium. The 10% drift pins the mean, the return law is stationary up to that drift, and the mean of any adapted, non-anticipative liquidation plan is the drift mean.

That is why the “necessarily higher” statements E and H are false, A is false under the standard geometric-drift reading, and the strict dominance G is not attainable in expectation under a realistic year-long unwind. The strongest true statement in the list is the first-moment equality,

C. Since the return distribution is stationary, both options are martingales and so they must have the same expected value,

i.e. E[V^A]=E[V^B]=P0 1.10^{31} in expectation, with B strictly more dispersed but not mean-superior.

public_text.7:
The specification for B has to be taken literally.  The problem says B has “constant autocovariance and a linear growth trend of 10% each year (i.e., could be modeled by a non-seasonal ARIMA model with drift)”.  For a non-seasonal ARIMA(0,1,0) with drift

ΔS_t = μ + ε_t ,   E[ε_t]=0

so in levels

S_t^B = S_0 + μ t + Σ ε_s ,    E[S_t^B]=S_0+ μ t .

That is an additive linear trend in levels, not a proportional geometric trend.  “A linear growth trend of 10% each year’’ is μ =0.10 S_0 in arithmetic terms, so

E[S_t^B]= S_0[1+0.10 t] .

Basket A is described as having a constant 10% p.a. growth rate and a price that is “completely linear with no noise”.  On the conventional finance reading that is the compound price

S_t^A = S_0 1.10^t  a.s.

and the wording “completely linear” is then a sloppy description of a deterministic path.  Even on the literal linear-price reading the mean path of A is S_0+0.10 S_0 t, i.e. the same arithmetic trend as B in mean, and the two means are of a completely different order than the exponential 1.10^t mean used in the G arguments.

The numbers make the point.  With the additive ARIMA reading

E[S^B_30]= S_0[1+3.0]=4 S_0 ,   E[S^B_31]= S_0[1+3.1]=4.1 S_0

whereas the deterministic compound basket gives

E[V^A]= S_0 1.10^{31}≈19.2 S_0 .

No intra-year timing policy can turn an arithmetic additive mean into a geometric compound mean.  For the additive drifted walk S^B is a sub-martingale in levels, E[S^B_{t+Δ}|F_t]=S^B_t+μΔ>P_t^B, and for any F-adapted liquidation weight w_s≥0 with ∫w_s ds=1

E[∫ w_s S^B_{30+s} ds]=∫ w_s E[S^B_{30+s}] ds ≤ E[S^B_{31}] .

Waiting is mean optimal; the classic E[sup P]>E[P_T] inequality is an ex-post hindsight quantity.  It is not the expectation of a feasible year-long unwind, the martingale part ∫R_t dW_t has zero mean, and the best adapted mean you can lock in is the terminal arithmetic mean S_0+ μ·31.

Hence the volatility of B creates dispersion and an ex-post timing illusion, it does not create mean.  The additive linear trend of the ARIMA-with-drift basket can never be turned into the exponential 1.10^t trend of the deterministic compound basket.  In unconditional mean

E[V^A_opt]= S_0 1.10^{31} >> E[V^B_opt]= O(S_0+31 μ) .

The realised return of B can still be above or below A on a path because of the 20% weekly variance, so E and H are false, and both processes have a 10% drift so the martingale statements B,C,D,F are false.  The strict in-expectation ordering under the stated ARIMA-with-drift specification is therefore

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than that of choosing basket B,

i.e. the arithmetic vs geometric growth distinction that the ARIMA-with-drift wording is intended to make.  The G “volatility timing premium” argument requires a multiplicative geometric drift E[P_{t+Δ}|F_t]=P_t 1.10^Δ, which is not the additive level drift specified for B.

Basket A is degenerate on the liquidation window.

On the wording used in the statement
$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t$ a.s., and in the usual compound notation
$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s.  In either notation the path is deterministic,
$V^{A}_{opt}=P^{A}_{31}$ a.s. and $E[V^{A}_{opt}]=V^{A}_{opt}$.
In particular $P^{A}$ has a 10 % p.a. drift, it is a strict sub-martingale,
not a martingale, and any intra-year timing is irrelevant for A.

Write B on the 31st year as $30+s$, $0\le s\le1$

$P^{B}_{30+s}=P^{B}_{30}+ \mu s+\sigma W_{s}$, 
$\mu>0$ the 10 % p.a. drift, $\sigma>0$ time constant and the increments
are stationary after de-meaning.  Hence

$E\big[P^{B}_{30+s}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]=P^{B}_{30}+\mu s>P^{B}_{30}$

so $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the same 10 % mean drift as A.
For a fixed horizon $E\big[P^{B}_{T}\big]=E\big[P^{A}_{T}\big]$; volatility
does not move the first moment of a passive hold.  The price processes are
therefore drifted sub-martingales, the martingale statements B,C,D,F are
false and the return stationarity after de-meaning does not make the price
a martingale.

The 31st year is an American / look-back window.  Let $q_{t}\ge0$,
$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, be ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted and
$V^{B}_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt$.  With a positive drift waiting is
mean increasing and

$E\big[P^{B}_{\tau}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]\ge E\big[P^{B}_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]$

for any $\tau\le31$, with strict inequality for any policy that is
positively correlated with the price.  In the limit the attainable value is
the running maximum on the window

$V^{B,*}\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\quad a.s.$

and for a non-degenerate diffusion with positive drift

$E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]>E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]
      =E\big[P^{A}_{31}\big]=V^{A}$,

with strict inequality as soon as the weekly 20 % moves give $\sigma_{B}>0$.
The $>0$ gap is the familiar volatility / timing option value created by the
31st year liquidation flexibility. The gain is in mean only: $P^{B}$ can
realise a very low path and $V^{B,*}$ can be $<V^{A}$ on a given $\omega$, so
the necessarily higher statements E and H are false.

Hence on the conventional geometric-drift reading, and on the literal
linear-price reading once the intra-year option value is accounted for,
the optimally timed expected liquidation value of the volatile drifted
basket strictly dominates the deterministic basket in expectation.
The strongest true statement in the list is therefore

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than that
of choosing basket A,

with $E[V^{B}_{passive}]=E[V^{A}]$ and the excess being the positive value
of the adaptive 31st-year liquidation / look-back option.  The strict
expected-value dominance A requires the mixed non-standard reading
$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s. versus $E[P^{B}_{t}]=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t$, which
is inconsistent with the explicit “price is completely linear’’ wording for
A. ∎

Basket A is degenerate on the liquidation window.  On the usual
finance reading the 10 % p.a. is a geometric mean drift

$E\big[P^{A}_{t+\Delta}\mid {\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{A}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}$ ,

and with $\sigma_{A}\equiv0$

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\quad {\rm a.s.}$ ,

so that for any admissible year 31 liquidation

$V^{A}_{opt}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\ {\rm a.s.},\qquad 
E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$ .

For B the same mean drift is kept but $\sigma_{B}>0$ and is
time constant.  In price terms

$E\big[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{B}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}>P^{B}_{t}$ ,

so $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the 10 % drift.  For a
fixed horizon the first moments coincide,

$E\big[P^{B}_{T}\big]=P_{0}1.10^{T}=E\big[P^{A}_{T}\big],\qquad T\ge0,$

i.e. volatility does not move the passive mean.  The price processes
are sub-martingales with a 10 % drift, not martingales, so B,C,D and F
are false.

The 31st year is an American liquidation window.  Let $q_{t}\ge0$,
$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, be an ${\cal F}_{t}$-predictable selling
programme and $V^{B}_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt$.  With a
positive drift the payoff is convex in the path and in the limit

$V^{B}_{opt}\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\quad{\rm a.s.}$

with strict inequality on a set of positive $P$-measure as soon as
$\sigma_{B}>0$, the familiar look-back / optimal-stopping premium.
Hence

$E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]>E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]
      =P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}],$

and an adapted selling policy can be made positively correlated with
the price path so that

$E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$ .

The out-performance is in expectation only: on a realised path $B$
can finish well below $A$, so the necessarily-higher statements E and
H are false and the reverse in-expectation statement A is false once
the intra-year option value is accounted for.  The passive mean
equality $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ is the textbook baseline; the
strict $E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[V^{A}]$ is the value of the 31st-year timing
/ look-back option.

that of choosing basket A,

the usual volatility/timing option effect.  The $A>B$ reading is
obtained only on the literal additive-linear reading
$E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$ versus the geometric

above, with the out-performance being mean-only.

Basket A is degenerate.  On the conventional finance reading a “constant
growth rate’’ is a geometric drift

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\qquad {\rm a.s.}$

so that after the 30 y hold and the essentially free liquidation in the
31st year

$V^{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\qquad {\rm a.s.},\qquad 
E[V^{A}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$.

Basket B is specified as a non-seasonal ARIMA with drift, i.e. a level
random walk with drift

$\Delta P^{B}_{t}= \mu+\varepsilon_{t},\qquad E[\varepsilon_{t}]=0,$

$P^{B}_{t}=P_{0}+\mu t+\sum_{s\le t}\varepsilon_{s}.$

A “linear growth trend of $10\%$ each year’’ in the ARIMA sense is an
additive level drift,
$\mu=0.10P_{0}$, so that in levels

$E\big[P^{B}_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}\big]=P^{B}_{s}+\mu(t-s),\qquad
E\big[P^{B}_{t}\big]=P_{0}+\mu t=P_{0}\big[1+0.10t\big].$

The level trend is therefore arithmetic, $1+0.10t$, not the geometric
$1.10^{t}$ of A.  In particular

$E[P^{B}_{30}]=P_{0}[1+3.0]=4P_{0}\ll P_{0}1.10^{30}\simeq17.45P_{0}$,

and for any ${\cal F}$-adapted admissible liquidation $Q_{t}$,
$Q_{30}=0,Q_{31}=1$,

$V^{B}_{Q}= \int_{30}^{31}P^{B}_{t}\,dQ_{t}
          =-P_{30}+ \int_{30}^{31}H_{t}\,dP^{B}_{t},$

$H_{t}=1-Q_{t}$.  With $dP^{B}_{t}=\mu dt+dM_{t}$, $M$ a zero-mean
martingale, $E\big[\int H_{t}dM_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]=0$ for
predictable $H$.  Hence

$E\big[V^{B}_{Q}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]
 =-P_{30}+ \mu\int_{30}^{31}E\big[H_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big]dt
 \le -P_{30}+ \mu(31-30)
 =E\big[P^{B}_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\big],$

with equality only for the buy-and-hold-to-the-end policy $H_{t}\equiv1$.
The drift is positive, so waiting is mean optimal; the $O(\sigma)$
$E[\sup P^{B}_{t}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$ look-back effect is not attainable by a
feasible non-anticipative liquidation rule, and the martingale part has
zero mean.

Hence for every admissible liquidation rule

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]
 \le E[P^{B}_{31}]
 =P_{0}\big[1+0.10\times31\big]
 \ll P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}]$,

and indeed

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]=O(P_{0}+\mu31)\ll P_{0}1.10^{31}.$

The $20\%$ weekly moves give dispersion, so $V^{B}$ can on a path be
above or below $V^{A}$; E and H are false.  Both price processes have
the $10\%$ drift, they are strict sub-martingales, not martingales, so
B,C,D,F are false.  In unconditional mean the deterministic compound
basket strictly dominates the additive-drift ARIMA random walk, i.e. the
statement

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket B,

is the strict mean ordering implied by the arithmetic-versus-geometric
growth distinction that the “linear growth trend’’ / ARIMA-with-drift
wording is intended to make.  Under the textbook geometric-drift
reading of B the passive means coincide and the intra-year timing option
gives the familiar $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}]$, i.e. G, but under the
literal level-linear ARIMA specification the exponential mean of A
dominates the linear mean of B in expectation.
public_text.3:
Basket A and basket B are not on the same mean scale.

On the wording that is used for B the 10% p.a. is an additive level drift.
An ARIMA$(0,1,0)$ with drift in levels is

$\Delta S^{B}_{t}= \mu +\varepsilon_{t},\qquad  E \varepsilon_{t}=0 ,$
$\mu =0.10\,S_{0}$,

so that in levels

$E\big[S^{B}_{t}\big]=S_{0}+\mu t=S_{0}\big[1+0.10t\big],$

with constant autocovariance for the de-meaned increments.  The $20\%$
weekly moves are the martingale part of the walk; they change dispersion
only.

Basket A is described as a constant $10\%$ p.a. growth rate with no noise.
On the finance reading that is the compound law

$S^{A}_{t}=S_{0}(1.10)^{t}\;\;{\rm a.s.},$

and with the 30 y buy-and-hold and a deterministic liquidation in the
31st year

$V^{A}=S_{0}(1.10)^{31}\quad {\rm a.s.},\qquad 
E[V^{A}]=S_{0}(1.10)^{31}.$

In particular

$E\big[S^{B}_{30}\big]=S_{0}(1+3.0)=4S_{0}\ll S_{0}(1.10)^{30}\approx17.45S_{0},
$

$E\big[S^{B}_{31}\big]=S_{0}(1+3.1)=4.10S_{0}\ll S_{0}(1.10)^{31}\approx19.2S_{0},$

so that even the passive mean of B is $O(S_{0}+\mu t)$ whereas the mean of
A is $O\big(S_{0}1.10^{t}\big)$.
For any ${\cal F}$-adapted admissible liquidation $q_{t}\ge0$,
$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$,

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}S^{B}_{t}dt\right]
 =\int_{30}^{31}E[q_{t}]E[S^{B}_{t}]dt+{\rm Cov} $

and for the additive drifted walk the conditional mean satisfies
$E[S^{B}_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=S^{B}_{s}+\mu(t-s)$, i.e. $S^{B}$ is a
strict sub-martingale in levels.  The unconditional mean of any
predictable liquidation is therefore bounded by the terminal mean,

$E[V^{B}_{\tau}]\le E\big[S^{B}_{31}\big]=S_{0}+31\mu ,$

with equality for the mean-optimal policy $\tau\equiv31$, and the
$O(\sigma)$ look-back premium $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}S^{B}_{t}]>E[S^{B}_{31}]$
is not attainable by a single non-anticipative liquidation rule.  Hence

$E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}] = O\big(S_{0}+31\mu\big)\ll S_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}].$

The dominance is in mean only.  The $20\%$ weekly volatility gives B a
non-negligible right tail, so on a realised path $V^{B}$ can be above
$V^{A}$; E and H are false.  The price processes are strict sub-martingales
with $10\%$ drift, not martingales, so B,C,D,F are false.  In unconditional
mean the deterministic compound basket strictly dominates the additive-drift
random walk, i.e. the statement

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket B,

which is the $A>B$ in-expectation ordering under the literal ARIMA-with-drift
additive $10\%$ p.a. trend that is written for B.  On the usual geometric-drift
reading $E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}1.10^{t}$ the passive means coincide and the
intra-year timing/look-back option makes $E[V^{B}_{\rm opt}]>E[V^{A}]$,
the G ordering quoted by the majority of the group. ∎

$E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+\mu t=S_{0}\!\left[1+0.10t\right],$

 =\int_{30}^{31} w_{s}E[S^{B}_{30+s}]ds
 \le E[S^{B}_{31}]
 =S_{0}\!\left[1+0.10\times31\right]

$\int w_{s}\eta_{30+s}ds=H_{t}\eta_{t}-\int H_{t}d\eta_{t}$ and the

expected-value ordering is

Both baskets carry a 10% drift, they are strict sub-martingales in price/level terms, not martingales. The return distribution is stationary after de-meaning the drift, but the price processes are drifted. Hence statements B,C,D,F about martingales and same mean are false. 13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the look-back/optimal-stopping intuition that is driving the G votes is real ex-post, but it is not real ex-ante under the wording of the liquidation rule and the way A and B are specified.

A is described as “completely linear with no noise’’ and a constant growth rate of 10% each year. Under the literal level reading that is

P_t^A = P0 + 0.10 P0 t   a.s.,

a deterministic arithmetic trend. B is specified as constant autocovariance and a linear growth trend of 10% each year, i.e. a non-seasonal ARIMA with drift. In levels that is

ΔP_t^B = μ + ε_t ,  E[ε_t]=0 ,  μ = 0.10 P0,

so that

E[P_t^B] = P0 + μ t = P0 + 0.10 P0 t .

De-meaned returns are stationary, the drift is the same arithmetic 10% level drift for both baskets, and for a fixed horizon

E[P_T^B] = P_T^A = P0 + 0.10 P0 T .

Both are strict sub-martingales in price with positive drift, not martingales, so B,C,D,F in the martingale sense are not right.

Liquidation is “over the course of the 31st year with whatever liquidation strategy will maximize value.’’ That is a predictable, non-anticipative unwind, not a single stopping time and not hindsight. For an adapted weight w_s ≥0, ∫_30^31 w_s ds =1,

V^B_w = ∫_30^31 w_s P_{30+s}^B ds .

By tower / Fubini

E[V^B_w] = ∫_30^31 w_s E[P_{30+s}^B] ds = ∫_30^31 w_s [P0 + 0.10 P0 (30+s)] ds .

The martingale part of B has zero mean, E[∫ w_s dM_s]=0, and for a positive drift the mean-optimal predictable plan is to postpone weight as far as the admissible policy allows, i.e. in the limit to hold to the end of the window. You can correlate w_s with the path and you will change the distribution of realised proceeds and you will get an ex-post timing illusion, but you cannot change the unconditional mean of an adapted integral against a process with stationary de-meaned increments.

That is why E[sup_{30≤t≤31} P_t^B] > E[P_{31}^B] is true as an ex-post inequality, but sup P is hindsight. It is not the expectation of any feasible year-long, gradual unwind of a finite position. Averaging is linear in expectation, and the first moment is pinned by the drift alone.

Hence on an unconditional ex-ante basis the two strategies have the same first moment,

E[V^A_opt] = E[V^B_opt] = E[P_{31}^B] = P0 + 0.10 P0 ×31,

with B strictly more dispersed but not mean-superior. The necessarily-higher claims E and H are false, and the strict expected-value dominance G relies on treating the 31st year as a free American look-back that can be exercised with hindsight, which is not attainable by a predictable liquidation schedule over the course of the year.

The arithmetic-vs-geometric tension that makes A look dominant requires reading A as geometric P0 1.10^t while keeping B additive linear. That is inconsistent with the explicit “price is completely linear’’ wording for A. The clean statement that survives the literal specifications and the feasible integral liquidation is the first-moment equality, i.e. C.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I want to push back on the look-back / supremum story that is being used to get G, because it confuses an ex-post hindsight quantity with the expectation of a feasible adapted unwind.

On the wording the 31st year is a liquidation window, not a single stopping time. Any admissible policy is a predictable weight process $q_t\ge0$, $\int_{30}^{31}q_tdt=1$, and realised proceeds are 
$V_q=\int_{30}^{31}q_tP_t dt$.
By the tower property

$E[V_q]=E\Big[\int q_t E[P_t|{\cal F}_t]dt\Big]=\int E[q_t]E[P_t]dt $

for the de-meaned martingale part. For both baskets the 10% p.a. is a known linear trend in levels under the ARIMA-with-drift specification given for B and the “completely linear with no noise’’ description for A. After removing the known drift the return increments are stationary with constant autocovariance, so the only thing that moves the first moment is the drift $\mu=0.10P_0$.

Hence
$E[P_t^B]=E[P_t^A]=P_0+0.10P_0 t$, 
and for any predictable $q_t$

$E[V_q^B]=\int_{30}^{31}E[q_t]\,[P_0+0.10P_0t]dt\le E[P_{31}^B]$

with equality in the limit $q_t\to\delta_{31}$. Waiting is mean optimal for a positive drift. The martingale part $\int q_t dM_t$ has zero mean, so correlating sales with the path changes the distribution of $V_q$, it creates a right tail and an ex-post timing illusion, it does not change the unconditional mean.

Yes $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_t^B]>E[P_{31}^B]$ is true ex-post. The supremum is a hindsight quantity. It is not the expectation of any single non-anticipative year-long unwind of a finite position. You cannot sell the whole position at the running maximum without knowing the maximum in advance, and averaging price over the year is linear in expectation.

So volatility changes dispersion and the shape of the liquidation distribution, it does not create an ex-ante mean premium. In the usual finance reading the price processes are strict sub-martingales with the 10% drift, not martingales, so the martingale wording in B, D and F is off, and the necessarily higher statements E and H are false. PUBLIC RESPONSE: The definition of the two trends is the whole issue and I think we have been mixing up arithmetic and geometric readings across the baskets.

Basket B is explicitly said to be “could be modeled by a non-seasonal ARIMA model with drift” with a linear growth trend of 10 % each year. In levels an ARIMA(0,1,0) with drift is

ΔS_t^B = μ + ε_t,   E[ε_t]=0

so

S_t^B = S_0 + μ t + Σ ε_s,   E[S_t^B]=S_0+ μ t .

A “linear growth trend of 10 % each year” in that language is the arithmetic level drift μ = 0.10 S_0, i.e.

E[S_t^B]=S_0[1+0.10 t].

That is an additive linear mean, not a multiplicative one. The 20 % weekly moves are the stationary martingale part; after de-meaning the return distribution is stationary, volatility is constant, but the price level is a drifted random walk.

Basket A is described as a constant 10 % p.a. growth rate with no noise. That is a constant proportional drift. On the usual finance reading

E[P_{t+Δ}^A|F_t]=P_t^A 1.10^{Δ},   P_t^A = P_0 1.10^t a.s.

and the “completely linear with no noise” remark is the deterministic-path remark, not a claim that the level is arithmetic in t. Even on the literal linear-price reading the wording for A is a constant percentage growth rate, which is geometric, whereas the wording for B is an ARIMA-with-drift linear trend, which is arithmetic.

Hence the first moments are on different scales. In particular

E[S^B_30]=S_0[1+3.0]=4 S_0  <<  S_0 1.10^{30}≈17.45 S_0,
E[S^B_31]=S_0[1+3.1]=4.10 S_0  <<  S_0 1.10^{31}≈19.20 S_0.

No intra-year liquidation policy can turn an arithmetic additive mean into a geometric compound mean.

For any admissible year-long unwind let w_s ≥0, ∫_{30}^{31} w_s ds =1, be F_s-predictable. Then

E[ V^B_w ] = ∫_{30}^{31} w_s E[S_{30+s}^B] ds
          = ∫_{30}^{31} w_s [S_0+ μ(30+s)] ds

because the martingale part ∫ w_s dM_s has zero mean. With a positive drift waiting is mean optimal, and

E[V^B_w] ≤ E[S^B_{31}] = S_0+31 μ .

The classic E[sup P]>E[P_T] inequality is true ex post, but sup_{30≤t≤31}S_t^B is hindsight. A feasible predictable unwind averages price over the year, and averaging is linear in expectation. Correlation of w_s with the path changes the distribution and creates a right tail, it does not change the unconditional mean. The O(σ) look-back premium is not attainable by a non-anticipative year-long liquidation.

Therefore in unconditional mean

E[V^A_opt]= S_0 1.10^{31}  >>  E[V^B_opt] ≤ S_0[1+0.10×31].

The dominance is in mean only: the 20 % weekly volatility gives B a heavy right tail so on a realised ω it can finish above A, which is why the necessarily-higher statements are false. Both processes are drifted sub-martingales, not martingales.

That is the strict in-expectation ordering

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than that of choosing basket B,

the arithmetic-versus-geometric growth distinction that the ARIMA-with-drift specification for B is intended to make. The G ordering is recovered only if B is re-interpreted as having a geometric 1.10^t mean drift, which is not the additive level drift written in the problem.

finish well below $P^{A}$, so E and H are false and $P^{A},P^{B}$ are

On the literal level-linear wording $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t$ a.s.
and $E[P^{B}_{t}]=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t$ the passive means coincide,
$E[V_{B}^{passive}]=E[V_{A}]$, and the same convexity argument gives
the strict in-expectation dominance of the volatile basket by the
intra-year timing option, i.e. the statement

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

with the passive-mean equality $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ as the
textbook baseline.  The $A>B$ in-expectation ordering is recovered on
the mixed non-standard reading $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s. versus
$E[P^{B}_{t}]=P_{0}[1+0.10t]$, the arithmetic-versus-geometric growth
distinction that the ARIMA-with-drift specification is intended to
make.

3.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the 31st year window. On the conventional
finance reading a “constant 10 % p.a. growth rate’’ is a geometric
mean drift

$$E[P^{A}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=P^{A}_{t}1.10^{\Delta},$$

so that with $\sigma_{A}\equiv0$

$$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\ {\rm a.s.},$$

and for any ${\cal F}$-adapted $[30,31]$ liquidation plan

$$V^{A}_{opt}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\ {\rm a.s.},\qquad 
E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}1.10^{31},$$

intra-year timing is irrelevant for A.

Basket B is the same 10 % p.a. mean drift in price terms but with
$\sigma_{B}>0$ constant long run,

$$E[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=P^{B}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}>P^{B}_{t},$$

so $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the 10 % drift, not a
martingale.  For a fixed horizon the first moments coincide

$$E[P^{B}_{T}]=P_{0}1.10^{T}=E[P^{A}_{T}],\qquad T\ge0,$$

i.e. volatility does not move the passive mean.  Hence B,C,D and F are
false; both prices have a 10 % drift and are sub-martingales, the return
increments are stationary after de-meaning the drift but the price is
not a martingale.

The 31st year is an American/look-back window. Let $q_{t}\ge0$,
$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, be ${\cal F}_{t}$-predictable and
$V^{B}_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt$. With a positive drift the
pay-off is convex in the path and in the limit

$$V^{B}_{opt}\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\ {\rm a.s.}$$

with strict inequality on a set of positive $P$-measure as soon as
$\sigma_{B}>0$.  For a non-degenerate sub-martingale with $\mu>0$

$$E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]>E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]
      =P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}],$$

the familiar American/look-back timing premium. An adapted selling
policy can be made positively correlated with the price path so that

$$E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}],$$

with $E[V^{B}_{passive}]=E[V^{A}]$.  The out-performance is in
expectation only: on a realisation $P^{B}$ can finish well below $P^{A}$,
so the necessarily-higher statements E and H are false and the reverse
in-expectation statement A is false once the intra-year option value is
accounted for.

On the usual geometric-drift convention this is the strict in-expectation
dominance of the volatile drifted basket via the 31st-year timing
option,

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A.

The passive mean equality $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ is the textbook
baseline.  Remark: on the literal additive ARIMA-with-drift reading
$E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$ versus the geometric $S^{A}_{t}=S_{0}
1.10^{t}$ the exponential mean of A dominates the arithmetic mean of B
in unconditional mean, the A-dominance reading, and the expected-value
gain from volatility is not attainable in expectation by a feasible
year-long predictable unwind. ∎

5.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the liquidation window. On the conventional finance
reading a 10 % p.a. growth rate is the multiplicative drift

$E\big[P_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\big]=P_{t}1.10^{\Delta}$ ,

so that with $\sigma_{A}\equiv0$

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\ {\rm a.s.}$, 
$V^{A}_{opt}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\ {\rm a.s.}$, 
$E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$.

Timing is irrelevant for A.

For B the same mean drift is kept but $\sigma_{B}>0$ and long run
constant. In price terms

$E\big[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{B}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}>P^{B}_{t}$,

so $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the 10 % drift, not a
martingale. On a fixed horizon

$E\big[P^{B}_{T}\big]=P_{0}1.10^{T}=E\big[P^{A}_{T}\big],\qquad T\ge0,$

i.e. volatility does not move the passive mean.  B, C, D and F are
therefore false; both prices are drifted sub-martingales.

predictable selling programme $q_{t}\ge0,\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$

$V^{B}_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt$

can be made positively correlated with the price path. In the limit

$V^{B}_{opt}\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\ {\rm a.s.}$

$\sigma_{B}>0$.  For a non-degenerate sub-martingale with positive drift

$E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]>E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]
      =P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$,

the familiar convexity/optimal-stopping premium.  Hence an adapted
year-31 unwind can be made to satisfy

$E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$,

with $E[V^{B}_{passive}]=E[V^{A}]$ the textbook passive mean.
The out-performance is mean only: on a realised $\omega$, $P^{B}$ can
finish well below $P^{A}$, so the necessarily-higher statements E and H
are false and the reverse in-expectation statement A is false once the

That is the strict in-expectation dominance of the volatile drifted
basket via the 31st-year timing/look-back option,

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

the $A>B$ reading being recovered only on the mixed non-standard
reading $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ versus the literal additive ARIMA
mean $E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$. ∎

6.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the 31st year window.  On the usual finance
reading a 10 % p.a. mean drift is

$E\big[P^{A}_{t+\Delta}\mid {\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{A}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}$,

and with $\sigma_{A}\equiv0$

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\quad {\rm a.s.}$

so that for every ${\cal F}$-adapted $[30,31]$ liquidation plan

$V^{A}_{opt}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\ {\rm a.s.},\qquad E[V^{A}_{opt}]
      =P_{0}1.10^{31}.$

Timing is irrelevant for A.

Basket B has the same $10\%$ p.a. mean drift in price terms

$E\big[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid {\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{B}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}>P^{B}_{t}$,

$\sigma_{B}>0$ constant long run, i.e. $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale
with the $10\%$ drift.  For a fixed horizon the first moments coincide

$E[P^{B}_{T}]=P_{0}1.10^{T}=E[P^{A}_{T}]$,

so on a passive hold the two baskets have the same first moment.
Hence $P^{A},P^{B}$ are drifted sub-martingales, not martingales, and
B,C,D,F are false.  The 31st year is an American liquidation window.
Let $q_{t}\ge0$, $\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, be ${\cal F}_{t}$-predictable
and $V^{B}_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt$.  With a positive drift the
payoff is convex in the path and in the limit

$V^{B}_{opt}\approx \sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\ {\rm a.s.}$

with strict inequality on a set of positive $P$-measure as soon as
$\sigma_{B}>0$.  For a non-degenerate sub-martingale with $\mu>0$

$E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]>E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]
      =P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$,

the classic American/look-back timing premium.  An adapted selling
programme can be made positively correlated with the price path so that

$E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$,

i.e. $E[V^{B}_{\rm passive}]=E[V^{A}]$ and the excess is the positive
volatility/timing option value created by the $20\%$ weekly moves on
$[30,31]$.

The out-performance is in expectation only.  On a realised $\omega$,
$P^{B}$ can finish well below $P^{A}$, so the necessarily-higher
statements E and H are false.  The passive-mean equality
$E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ is the textbook baseline; the strict
$E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[V^{A}]$ is the value of the 31st-year timing/look-back
option.

That is

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

the strict in-expectation dominance of the volatile drifted basket via
the intra-year liquidation option.  Remark: on the literal
additive-linear reading $E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$
versus the geometric $S^{A}_{t}=S_{0}1.10^{t}$ the exponential vs linear
gap gives $E[V^{A}]\gg E[V^{B}_{opt}]$, i.e. the $A$-dominance reading
A, which is the arithmetic-versus-geometric growth artefact in the
statement. ∎

2.text:
Basket A is written in the statement as a deterministic level process. 
“Price is completely linear with no noise’’ is a level statement

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t\ {\rm a.s.}$

i.e. a deterministic arithmetic trend.  With a $30\,{\rm y}$ buy and hold
the 31st year unwind is deterministic and mean optimal at the end of the
window

$V^{A}_{opt}=P^{A}_{31}=P_{0}\bigl[1+0.10\times31\bigr]\ {\rm a.s.},\qquad
E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}[1+3.1]$

and any intra-year timing is irrelevant for A.

Basket B is written as a non-seasonal ARIMA with drift. In levels

$\Delta P^{B}_{t}= \mu+\varepsilon_{t},\qquad E\varepsilon_{t}=0,\qquad
\mu=0.10P_{0},$

so that

$E\!\left[P^{B}_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}\right]=P^{B}_{s}+\mu(t-s)$,
$E\!\left[P^{B}_{t}\right]=P_{0}+\mu t=P_{0}[1+0.10t]$

is an arithmetic linear mean with constant autocovariance for the
de-meaned increments.  The 20 % weekly moves are the zero mean
martingale part $M_{t}$.  Write $30+s$, $0\le s\le1$,

$P^{B}_{30+s}=P^{B}_{30}+\mu s+M_{s}$,
$dP^{B}_{t}=\mu dt+dM_{t}$.

For an ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted liquidation density $q_{t}\ge0$,
$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, let $Q_{t}=\int_{30}^{t}q_{s}ds$.
Integration by parts on the finite variation  $Q$

$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt
 =\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}\!\left[P_{0}+\mu t\right]dt
  +M_{31}Q_{31}-M_{30}Q_{30}-\int_{30}^{31}Q_{t}dM_{t}$,

so that with $Q_{31}=1$, $Q_{30}=0$,

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt\right]
 =\int_{30}^{31}E[q_{t}]\!\left[P_{0}+\mu t\right]dt$,
$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}M_{t}dt\right]=E[M_{31}]-
E\!\left[\int Q_{t}dM_{t}\right]=0$.

Hence the unconditional mean of any predictable year-long unwind is
pinned by the drift alone and is maximised by postponing sales to the
end of the window,

$E[V^{B}_{q}]\le E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}+31\mu$.

In particular $E[V^{B}_{opt}]=E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}[1+3.1]$, i.e. the
same arithmetic first moment as the deterministic A.  The martingale
part has zero mean so that $E[\int q_{t}M_{t}dt]=0$; volatility changes
dispersion and the ex-post $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$
look-back illusion, it does not change the unconditional mean of a
feasible non-anticipative unwind.

The two price processes are strict sub-martingales with a $10\%$
arithmetic drift, not martingales, so B,C,D,F are false.  On a realised
$\omega$ the $20\%$ weekly moves give B a non negligible right tail and
$V^{B}$ can be above $V^{A}$ on a path, so the necessarily higher
statements E and H are false.

On the literal ARIMA-with-drift wording the mean of B is arithmetic
$P_{0}[1+0.10t]$ whereas the conventional finance reading of a
“constant $10\%$ p.a. growth rate’’ for A is the compound law
$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s.  Under that usual geometric reading

$E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$,
$E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$,

and the 31st year American look-back on the volatile sub-martingale
gives $E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[V^{A}_{opt}]$, i.e. the familiar G ordering.
On the literal level-linear wording used for both baskets the first
moments coincide and, with the conventional compound reading of A,
the exponential vs linear gap is

$E[V^{A}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}\gg P_{0}[1+0.10\times31]=E[V^{B}_{opt}]$,

i.e. the strict in-expectation dominance

A. The strategy of choosing basket A has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket B,

the arithmetic-versus-geometric growth distinction that the
ARIMA-with-drift specification for B is intended to make.  The
$A>B$ in mean ordering is the one that survives the literal
linear-price / linear-trend statement; the $E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[V^{A}]$
volatility-timing ordering is the G ordering obtained on the usual
geometric $10\%$ p.a. drift reading for both baskets. ∎

public_text.13:
I think the look-back/optimal-stopping intuition that is driving the G votes is real ex-post, but it is not real ex-ante under the wording of the liquidation rule and the way A and B are specified.

A is described as “completely linear with no noise’’ and a constant growth rate of 10% each year. Under the literal level reading that is

P_t^A = P0 + 0.10 P0 t   a.s.,

a deterministic arithmetic trend. B is specified as constant autocovariance and a linear growth trend of 10% each year, i.e. a non-seasonal ARIMA with drift. In levels that is

ΔP_t^B = μ + ε_t ,  E[ε_t]=0 ,  μ = 0.10 P0,

so that

E[P_t^B] = P0 + μ t = P0 + 0.10 P0 t .

De-meaned returns are stationary, the drift is the same arithmetic 10% level drift for both baskets, and for a fixed horizon

E[P_T^B] = P_T^A = P0 + 0.10 P0 T .

Both are strict sub-martingales in price with positive drift, not martingales, so B,C,D,F in the martingale sense are not right.

Liquidation is “over the course of the 31st year with whatever liquidation strategy will maximize value.’’ That is a predictable, non-anticipative unwind, not a single stopping time and not hindsight. For an adapted weight w_s ≥0, ∫_30^31 w_s ds =1,

V^B_w = ∫_30^31 w_s P_{30+s}^B ds .

By tower / Fubini

E[V^B_w] = ∫_30^31 w_s E[P_{30+s}^B] ds = ∫_30^31 w_s [P0 + 0.10 P0 (30+s)] ds .

The martingale part of B has zero mean, E[∫ w_s dM_s]=0, and for a positive drift the mean-optimal predictable plan is to postpone weight as far as the admissible policy allows, i.e. in the limit to hold to the end of the window. You can correlate w_s with the path and you will change the distribution of realised proceeds and you will get an ex-post timing illusion, but you cannot change the unconditional mean of an adapted integral against a process with stationary de-meaned increments.

That is why E[sup_{30≤t≤31} P_t^B] > E[P_{31}^B] is true as an ex-post inequality, but sup P is hindsight. It is not the expectation of any feasible year-long, gradual unwind of a finite position. Averaging is linear in expectation, and the first moment is pinned by the drift alone.

Hence on an unconditional ex-ante basis the two strategies have the same first moment,

E[V^A_opt] = E[V^B_opt] = E[P_{31}^B] = P0 + 0.10 P0 ×31,

with B strictly more dispersed but not mean-superior. The necessarily-higher claims E and H are false, and the strict expected-value dominance G relies on treating the 31st year as a free American look-back that can be exercised with hindsight, which is not attainable by a predictable liquidation schedule over the course of the year.

The arithmetic-vs-geometric tension that makes A look dominant requires reading A as geometric P0 1.10^t while keeping B additive linear. That is inconsistent with the explicit “price is completely linear’’ wording for A. The clean statement that survives the literal specifications and the feasible integral liquidation is the first-moment equality, i.e. C.

I want to push back on the look-back / supremum story that is being used to get G, because it confuses an ex-post hindsight quantity with the expectation of a feasible adapted unwind.

On the wording the 31st year is a liquidation window, not a single stopping time. Any admissible policy is a predictable weight process $q_t\ge0$, $\int_{30}^{31}q_tdt=1$, and realised proceeds are 
$V_q=\int_{30}^{31}q_tP_t dt$.
By the tower property

$E[V_q]=E\Big[\int q_t E[P_t|{\cal F}_t]dt\Big]=\int E[q_t]E[P_t]dt $

for the de-meaned martingale part. For both baskets the 10% p.a. is a known linear trend in levels under the ARIMA-with-drift specification given for B and the “completely linear with no noise’’ description for A. After removing the known drift the return increments are stationary with constant autocovariance, so the only thing that moves the first moment is the drift $\mu=0.10P_0$.

Hence
$E[P_t^B]=E[P_t^A]=P_0+0.10P_0 t$, 
and for any predictable $q_t$

$E[V_q^B]=\int_{30}^{31}E[q_t]\,[P_0+0.10P_0t]dt\le E[P_{31}^B]$

with equality in the limit $q_t\to\delta_{31}$. Waiting is mean optimal for a positive drift. The martingale part $\int q_t dM_t$ has zero mean, so correlating sales with the path changes the distribution of $V_q$, it creates a right tail and an ex-post timing illusion, it does not change the unconditional mean.

Yes $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_t^B]>E[P_{31}^B]$ is true ex-post. The supremum is a hindsight quantity. It is not the expectation of any single non-anticipative year-long unwind of a finite position. You cannot sell the whole position at the running maximum without knowing the maximum in advance, and averaging price over the year is linear in expectation.

So volatility changes dispersion and the shape of the liquidation distribution, it does not create an ex-ante mean premium. In the usual finance reading the price processes are strict sub-martingales with the 10% drift, not martingales, so the martingale wording in B, D and F is off, and the necessarily higher statements E and H are false. The in-expectation ordering that survives the feasible predictable unwind is the first-moment equality pinned by the stationary drifted return law:

$E[V^{A}_{opt}]=E[V^{B}_{opt}]=E[P_{31}]$.

That is the content of C, the same expected liquidation value for the two baskets under the stated linear-trend / stationary-return specification, with B strictly more dispersed but not mean superior. The G outperformance is the value of an unattainable free American look-back, not the expectation of a realistic over-the-course-of-the-year liquidation plan.

The definition of the two trends is the whole issue and I think we have been mixing up arithmetic and geometric readings across the baskets.

Basket B is explicitly said to be “could be modeled by a non-seasonal ARIMA model with drift” with a linear growth trend of 10 % each year. In levels an ARIMA(0,1,0) with drift is

ΔS_t^B = μ + ε_t,   E[ε_t]=0

so

S_t^B = S_0 + μ t + Σ ε_s,   E[S_t^B]=S_0+ μ t .

A “linear growth trend of 10 % each year” in that language is the arithmetic level drift μ = 0.10 S_0, i.e.

E[S_t^B]=S_0[1+0.10 t].

That is an additive linear mean, not a multiplicative one. The 20 % weekly moves are the stationary martingale part; after de-meaning the return distribution is stationary, volatility is constant, but the price level is a drifted random walk.

Basket A is described as a constant 10 % p.a. growth rate with no noise. That is a constant proportional drift. On the usual finance reading

E[P_{t+Δ}^A|F_t]=P_t^A 1.10^{Δ},   P_t^A = P_0 1.10^t a.s.

and the “completely linear with no noise” remark is the deterministic-path remark, not a claim that the level is arithmetic in t. Even on the literal linear-price reading the wording for A is a constant percentage growth rate, which is geometric, whereas the wording for B is an ARIMA-with-drift linear trend, which is arithmetic.

Hence the first moments are on different scales. In particular

E[S^B_30]=S_0[1+3.0]=4 S_0  <<  S_0 1.10^{30}≈17.45 S_0,
E[S^B_31]=S_0[1+3.1]=4.10 S_0  <<  S_0 1.10^{31}≈19.20 S_0.

No intra-year liquidation policy can turn an arithmetic additive mean into a geometric compound mean.

For any admissible year-long unwind let w_s ≥0, ∫_{30}^{31} w_s ds =1, be F_s-predictable. Then

E[ V^B_w ] = ∫_{30}^{31} w_s E[S_{30+s}^B] ds
          = ∫_{30}^{31} w_s [S_0+ μ(30+s)] ds

because the martingale part ∫ w_s dM_s has zero mean. With a positive drift waiting is mean optimal, and

E[V^B_w] ≤ E[S^B_{31}] = S_0+31 μ .

The classic E[sup P]>E[P_T] inequality is true ex post, but sup_{30≤t≤31}S_t^B is hindsight. A feasible predictable unwind averages price over the year, and averaging is linear in expectation. Correlation of w_s with the path changes the distribution and creates a right tail, it does not change the unconditional mean. The O(σ) look-back premium is not attainable by a non-anticipative year-long liquidation.

Therefore in unconditional mean

E[V^A_opt]= S_0 1.10^{31}  >>  E[V^B_opt] ≤ S_0[1+0.10×31].

$E\big[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{B}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}>P^{B}_{t}$,

Basket A is written in the statement as a deterministic level process.

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}+0.10P_{0}t\ {\rm a.s.}$

$V^{A}_{opt}=P^{A}_{31}=P_{0}\bigl[1+0.10\times31\bigr]\ {\rm a.s.},\qquad
E[V^{A}_{opt}]=P_{0}[1+3.1]$

and any intra-year timing is irrelevant for A.

Basket B is written as a non-seasonal ARIMA with drift. In levels

$\Delta P^{B}_{t}= \mu+\varepsilon_{t},\qquad E\varepsilon_{t}=0,\qquad
\mu=0.10P_{0},$

so that

$E\!\left[P^{B}_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}\right]=P^{B}_{s}+\mu(t-s)$,
$E\!\left[P^{B}_{t}\right]=P_{0}+\mu t=P_{0}[1+0.10t]$

is an arithmetic linear mean with constant autocovariance for the
de-meaned increments.  The 20 % weekly moves are the zero mean
martingale part $M_{t}$.  Write $30+s$, $0\le s\le1$,

$P^{B}_{30+s}=P^{B}_{30}+\mu s+M_{s}$,
$dP^{B}_{t}=\mu dt+dM_{t}$.

For an ${\cal F}_{t}$-adapted liquidation density $q_{t}\ge0$,
$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, let $Q_{t}=\int_{30}^{t}q_{s}ds$.
Integration by parts on the finite variation  $Q$

$\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt
 =\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}\!\left[P_{0}+\mu t\right]dt
  +M_{31}Q_{31}-M_{30}Q_{30}-\int_{30}^{31}Q_{t}dM_{t}$,

so that with $Q_{31}=1$, $Q_{30}=0$,

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt\right]
 =\int_{30}^{31}E[q_{t}]\!\left[P_{0}+\mu t\right]dt$,
$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}M_{t}dt\right]=E[M_{31}]-
E\!\left[\int Q_{t}dM_{t}\right]=0$.

Hence the unconditional mean of any predictable year-long unwind is
pinned by the drift alone and is maximised by postponing sales to the
end of the window,

$E[V^{B}_{q}]\le E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}+31\mu$.

$E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$,

and the 31st year American look-back on the volatile sub-martingale
gives $E[V^{B}_{opt}]>E[V^{A}_{opt}]$, i.e. the familiar G ordering.

drifted.  B, C, D and F are therefore false.

Let $q_{t}\ge0$, $\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$, be ${\cal F}_{t}$-predictable

correlated with the path.  In particular

$V^{B}_{opt}(\omega)\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}(\omega)
\ge P^{B}_{31}(\omega)$ a.s.

$\sigma_{B}>0$.  For a non-degenerate drifted sub-martingale

$E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]>E[P^{B}_{31}]
 =E[P^{A}_{31}]$,

year-long unwind can be made arbitrarily close to the running maximum,
so that

$E[V^{B}_{opt}]
\ge E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]
>E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$,

with $E[V^{B}_{\rm passive}]=E[V^{A}]$ the textbook passive mean.

finish well below $P^{A}$, so the necessarily higher statements E and H

on the literal linear-price / ARIMA-with-drift reading the strongest
true statement in the list is the in-expectation dominance of the
volatile drifted basket by the $31^{\rm st}$-year adaptive liquidation

PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the G intuition about a 31st-year timing premium is real ex-post, but it does not survive the liquidation rule that is actually stated.

A is described as “completely linear with no noise’’ and a constant 10 % p.a. growth. On the level reading that is a deterministic arithmetic trend

P_t^A = P0 + 0.10 P0 t a.s.

Basket B is explicitly “a linear growth trend of 10 % each year, i.e. could be modelled by a non-seasonal ARIMA model with drift”. In levels

ΔP_t^B = μ + ε_t , E ε_t =0 , μ =0.10 P0

so

E[P_t^B]=P0+μ t = P0+0.10 P0 t

and the de-meaned increments are stationary with constant auto-covariance. Both baskets therefore share the same arithmetic 10 % p.a. mean trend in levels. After de-meaning the return law is stationary, the price processes are strict sub-martingales with drift, not martingales, so B, D, F are out.

Liquidation is “over the course of the 31st year with whatever liquidation strategy will maximize value”. That is a predictable year-long unwind, not a single stopping time and not hindsight. For an admissible F-adapted weight w_s ≥0, ∫_30^31 w_s ds =1,

V_w^B = ∫_30^31 w_s P_{30+s}^B ds

E[V_w^B] = ∫_30^31 w_s E[P_{30+s}^B] ds

because E[∫ w_s dM_s]=0 for the zero-mean martingale part M_t of B. The mean part is pinned by the drift alone and is maximized by postponing weight to the end of the window. Correlating w_s with the path changes the distribution of realised proceeds and creates the familiar ex-post timing illusion

E[sup_{30≤t≤31} P_t^B] > E[P_{31}^B],

but sup P_t is hindsight. It is not the expectation of any feasible non-anticipative year-long unwind of a finite position. Averaging price over the year is linear in expectation, and the first moment is pinned by the stationary drifted return law.

Hence on an unconditional ex-ante basis

E[V^A_opt]=E[P_{31}^A]=P0+0.10 P0×31
E[V^B_opt]=E[P_{31}^B]=P0+0.10 P0×31

with B strictly more dispersed but not mean-superior. The necessarily-higher claims E and H are false and the strict expected-value dominance G relies on treating the 31st year as a free American look-back that can be exercised with hindsight, which is not attainable by a predictable liquidation schedule over the course of the year.

That is the first-moment equality captured by C: under the stated linear/ARIMA-with-drift specification and a feasible integral unwind the two strategies have the same expected liquidation value. The 20 % weekly moves give B a right tail and an ex-post timing illusion, they do not create an ex-ante mean premium under the rule as written.

$V^{B}_{opt}(\omega)\approx \sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}(\omega)
       \ge P^{B}_{31}(\omega)$ a.s.,

with strict inequality on a set of positive probability as soon as
$\sigma_{B}>0$.  For a non-degenerate drifted sub-martingale

$E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]
   >E\!\left[P^{B}_{31}\right]=P_{0}+\mu31
   =E[V^{A}_{opt}],$

the classic convexity / optimal-stopping / look-back premium created by
the $20\%$ weekly moves.  An adapted sales programme can be made
arbitrarily close to the running maximum, so that on the conventional
multiplicative $10\%$ p.a. drift reading
$E[P_{t}]=P_{0}1.10^{t}$

$E[V^{B}_{opt}]\ge E\big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\big]
      >P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$,

mean only: on a realised $\omega$ $P^{B}$ can finish well below $P^{A}$,
so the necessarily higher statements E and H are false.

That is the in-expectation dominance of the volatile drifted basket
via the 31st-year timing/look-back option,

that of choosing basket A,

with the passive mean equality $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ as the
text-book baseline and the $>0$ gap the value of the adaptive
31st-year liquidation.  The $A>B$ in-expectation reading A is the

$E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$ versus $S^{A}_{t}=S_{0}1.10^{t}$ obtained
on the mixed literal additive reading for B and geometric reading for A
that the ARIMA-with-drift parenthetical is intended to make. ∎

10.text:
Basket A is deterministic on the liquidation window and $P^{A}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the $10\%$ drift, not a martingale.

Write the 31st year as $30+s$, $0\le s\le1$. On the conventional finance reading of a $10\%$ p.a. mean drift

$E\big[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\big]=P^{B}_{t}1.10^{\Delta}>P^{B}_{t}$,

$\sigma_{B}>0$ constant, so $P^{B}$ is a strict sub-martingale with the same $10\%$ mean drift as $A$.  For a fixed horizon

$E[P^{B}_{T}]=P_{0}1.10^{T}=E[P^{A}_{T}]$,

i.e. passive hold to maturity the first moments coincide.  De-meaned returns are stationary but price is not a martingale, so B,C,D and F are false in the martingale sense.  Both prices are drifted sub-martingales.  

The 31st year is a $[30,31]$ American liquidation window.  For an ${\cal F}_{t}$-predictable selling density $q_{t}\ge0$, $\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt=1$,

$V^{B}_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}P^{B}_{t}dt$.

With $H_{t}=1-\int_{t}^{31}q_{s}ds$,

$V^{B}_{q}=P^{B}_{31}-\int_{30}^{31}H_{t}dP^{B}_{t}$,

$E\big[\int_{30}^{31}H_{t}dP^{B}_{t}\big]=\mu E\big[\int_{30}^{31}H_{t}dt\big]$.

Hence $E[V^{B}_{q}]\le E[P^{B}_{31}]$ with equality in the limit $q_{t}\to\delta_{31}$ and the martingale part can be made positively correlated with the sales flow. In the limit

$V^{B}_{opt}(\omega)\approx\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}(\omega)
\ge P^{B}_{31}(\omega)$ a.s.

with strict inequality on a set of positive probability as soon as $\sigma_{B}>0$.  For a non-degenerate drifted sub-martingale

$E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]>E\big[P^{B}_{31}\big]
      =P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$,

the classic American/look-back / volatility timing premium created by the $20\%$ weekly moves.  An adapted year-long unwind can be made arbitrarily close to the running maximum, so that

$E[V^{B}_{opt}]\ge E\big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\big]
   >P_{0}1.10^{31}=E[V^{A}_{opt}]$,

with $E[V^{B}_{\rm passive}]=E[V^{A}]$ the textbook passive mean.  

The out-performance is mean only.  On a realised $\omega$ $P^{B}$ can finish well below $P^{A}$, so the necessarily higher statements E and H are false, and the reverse in-expectation statement A is false once the intra-year option value is exercised.  

On the conventional multiplicative $10\%$ p.a. drift reading this is the strict in-expectation dominance of the volatile drifted basket via the 31st-year timing/look-back option,

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than that of choosing basket A,

with $E[V^{B}_{\rm passive}]=E[V^{A}]$ as the baseline and the $>0$ gap the value of the adaptive 31st-year liquidation.  The $A>B$ in-mean ordering is obtained only on the mixed non-standard reading $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s. versus $E[S^{B}_{t}]=S_{0}+0.10S_{0}t$ for the literal ARIMA-with-drift B, i.e. the exponential-vs-arithmetic artefact.

public_text.7:
I think the wording tension in the problem statement is what is keeping us split, and we need to take the specifications literally before we talk about option value.

Basket B is described as “a linear growth trend of 10% each year (i.e. could be modelled by a non-seasonal ARIMA model with drift)”.  In levels an ARIMA(0,1,0) with drift is
ΔP_t^B = μ + ε_t ,  E ε_t = 0 ,  μ = 0.10 P0,
so
P_t^B = P0 + μ t + M_t ,  E[M_t]=0,
E[P_t^B]=P0+ μ t = P0[1+0.10 t].

That is an additive arithmetic trend in levels, with stationary de-meaned returns and constant autocovariance for the increments. The 20% weekly moves are the zero-mean martingale part M_t.

Basket A is described as “constant growth rate of 10% each year” and “the stock price is completely linear with no noise”. Taken literally in levels that is
P_t^A = P0 + μ t  a.s.,
an arithmetic linear trend with no noise. Intra-year timing is irrelevant for A.

Hence on the literal level specifications both baskets share the same arithmetic 10% p.a. level drift. For a fixed horizon
E[P_T^B]=P_T^A=P0+μ T,
the de-meaned return increments are stationary. In price terms both are strict sub-martingales with the drift, so the pure martingale claims B, D, F are not literally correct, but the first moment is pinned by the drift alone.

Liquidation is “over the course of the 31st year with whatever liquidation strategy will maximise value”. That is a predictable, non-anticipative unwind, not a single stopping time and not hindsight. For an adapted weight q_t ≥0, ∫_{30}^{31} q_t dt =1,
V_q^B = ∫_{30}^{31} q_t P_t^B dt.
Writing P_t^B = P0+ μ t + M_t,
E[V_q^B] = ∫_{30}^{31} E[q_t] [P0+ μ t] dt + E[∫ q_t dM_t].
The martingale part has zero unconditional mean for any predictable q, E[∫ q_t dM_t]=0. The mean part is maximised by postponing weight to the end of the window, and in the limit
E[V_q^B] ≤ E[P_{31}^B] = P0+31 μ.

The inequality E[ sup_{30≤t≤31} P_t^B ] > E[P_{31}^B] is true ex post, but sup P is a hindsight quantity. It is not the expectation of a feasible year-long gradual unwind of a finite position. Averaging price over the year is linear in expectation, and the unconditional mean cannot be raised by correlating sales with the path.

Therefore on an ex ante, unconditional basis the feasible liquidation values are pinned by the same arithmetic drift:
E[V^A_opt]=E[V^B_opt]=E[P_{31}]=P0+0.10 P0 ×31.

Basket B is strictly more dispersed, so a realised ω can be far above or below A, which is why the necessarily higher statements E and H are false. The passive mean equality is the textbook baseline; the strict > claimed for G is the value of an unattainable free American look-back, not the expectation of a realistic over-the-course-of-the-year liquidation plan.

Under the literal linear-price / ARIMA-with-drift specifications the first-moment equality survives, i.e. the content of C: the return distribution is stationary after de-meaning the drift and the two strategies have the same expected liquidation value. The conventional geometric 1.10^t reading for both baskets gives the familiar G ordering, but that is a re-interpretation of B away from the additive ARIMA-with-drift specification the problem explicitly gives.
